newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus MP goes missing after protest.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus MP goes missing after protest.

text.p: A Cypriot MP taking part in a protest against British military exercises on a remote peninsula on the island has disappeared, police said on Tuesday.
"His family has filed a report that he is missing," a police spokesman said. "We are looking for him."

Marios Matsakis, an MP for the centre-right Democratic Party, was one of a party of 15 environmentalists who scattered in a firing range in the north western Akamas peninsula on Monday to delay the start of the exercises.

While all other activists were found and removed from the area, Matsakis and at least two other people are still missing, according to police and activists who took part in the demonstration. Matsakis's car is still parked in the area.
British troops, in the meantime, started week-long exercises with live ammunition, saying they have no indication there is anybody in the firing range, which covers six square km.
"Our understanding is that there are no persons on the range at the moment," bases spokesman Mervyn Wynne-Jones told Reuters.
Environmentalists have demanded the exercises end and the area be declared a national park.
The former state pathologist is usually reacheable via his mobile phone. He had it switched off.
"We have a strong police presence in the area to stop demonstrators entering the firing range and we are seeking Matsakis," the police spokesman said.

The exercises are being carried out by 30 soldiers from the British base of Episkopi on the south coast. The bases are allowed, under the island's 1960 treaty of establishment, to train in the area for up to 70 days a year.
"There were some protestors in the vicinity of the camp overnight but as far as we are aware all is quiet," said Wynne-Jones, adding he was not aware if one of the protesters was Matsakis.
Wynne-Jones said that before any firing starts a range clearance is carried out to ensure nobody is in the area.
"If anyone is seen (in the range) training will cease immediately," he said.
